title: Catherine wheel motif
subtitle: A classic spoke-and-fan geometric tile in DK cotton, 12 cm
excerpt: The Catherine wheel motif uses an eight-point star construction built from treble-cluster spokes alternating with fan shells, giving the tile its distinctive wheel-spoke appearance. Worked in two colours, the spokes and fans read as separate bands; in a single colour the geometry is subtler. Tiles at 12 cm into a striking radial-pattern throw.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), Catherine wheel stitch and motif chapter (Internet Archive). The Catherine wheel construction appears in several Edwardian pattern books as a named stitch for blankets and shawls.
heroPrompt: A Catherine wheel crochet motif in navy and cream DK cotton, showing the classic spoke-and-fan wheel pattern, photographed flat from above on natural linen in soft daylight. 12 cm, eight spokes clearly visible.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished Catherine wheel motif measures 12 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a steam-block.

chartDefinition.title: Catherine wheel motif
chartDefinition.caption: Three rounds from the magic ring. Round 1: eight treble-cluster spokes. Round 2: fan shells into the chain spaces between spokes. Round 3: a dc border that closes the outer ring.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three or more trebles worked into the same space and drawn together at the top. Forms the eight spokes of the Catherine wheel centre.
Five trebles worked into the same chain space, fanning outward. Fills the spaces between the spokes in round 2.

content.text: The Catherine wheel builds eight
treble cluster
spokes into the magic ring, then fills the spaces between them with
fan shells

in round 2. The alternation of upward-pointing cluster and outward-fanning shell creates the wheel appearance that gives the stitch its name. Two-colour working — cluster in one colour, shell in another — gives the sharpest read of the spoke structure.

The Catherine wheel appears in Weldon's Practical Crochet as both a repeat stitch for flat work and as a stand-alone circular motif. As a motif it tiles in a grid with small square spacers between, or joins edge to edge by whipstitching through matching border dc stitches.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 7 g of Colour A (spokes), 8 g of Colour B (fans and border) — all DK-weight cotton. A 4 mm crochet hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Blocking mat and pins.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished Catherine wheel motif measures 12 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a steam-block.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
treble cluster (3tr-cl) — three trebles drawn together. UK; US "3dc-cl".
shell (5tr in same sp) — fan of five trebles. UK and US shared.
Pattern
Round 1 — Colour A (spokes)

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr of first cluster). Work 2 more tr into the ring, draw together (3tr-cl). *Ch 2. Work 3tr-cl into the ring.* Repeat from * to * six more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of first cluster to join. Pull ring tail to close. (8 clusters, 8 ch-2 spaces.) Fasten off Colour A.
Round 2 — Colour B (fans)

Join Colour B to any ch-2 space. *Work 5tr into ch-2 sp (fan made). Ch 1. Dc into top of next cluster. Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * seven more times. Sl st to first tr to join. (8 fans of 5tr each, 8 dc, 16 ch-1 spaces.)
Round 3 — border

Ch 1. Dc into first tr. *Ch 1. Dc into next tr. Ch 1. Dc into next tr. Ch 1. Dc into next tr. Ch 1. Dc into ch-1 sp. Ch 1. Dc into cluster-top dc. Ch 1. Dc into next ch-1 sp.* Repeat from * to * seven more times. Sl st to first dc to join. Fasten off.

definition.title: Catherine wheel motif
definition.caption: Eight cluster spokes in round 1. Five-treble fan shells between spokes in round 2. Dc border in round 3.

content.text: Finishing
Fasten off and weave in all ends. Steam-block with pins at the outer dc border to flatten the fan shells fully. The fans are inclined to curl before blocking.
Joining
Join Catherine wheel motifs through the ch-1 spaces on the border by whipstitch through matching dc stitches. For a throw, alternate spoke colour between tiles for a checkerboard effect.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

The Catherine wheel works as a repeating flat stitch for scarves and shawls as well as a stand-alone motif. For a blanket border, a row of Catherine wheel stitches makes a bold edging. The sunburst motif (crochet-sunburst-motif-basic) uses the same cluster-spoke logic with six spokes instead of eight.
